acceptance: The depth gate counts only identities whose bundles are rankable by the same predicate the explorer uses (shared code or a parity test)
A test proves a partial/failed bundle does not count toward depth
The phase-aware cohort change (item throughput-corpus-cohort-depth-third-identity) and this predicate land together or in dependency order
context: 2026-10-04 throughput adversarial review. Reviewed the #2382 branch HEAD 938150a4f, its uncommitted validator change, and develop 8ed0c64e1.
description:
`cohort_platforms` in results-data/validate_corpus.py (205-224 on the #2382 branch) never looks at summary.queries.failed, summary.validation or throughput_test.status. Adding the SQLite bundle tpch_sf1_sqlite_sql_20261003_184424_5702d960.json (45 of 66 queries failed, throughput_test FAILED) would make the TPC-H SF1 throughput cohort reach 3 identities and pass. The explorer would then exclude that row from ranking (failed_queries and validation_not_clean in _project/scripts/explorer_pipeline/models.py:588-591), leaving 2 rankable engines.

The same SQLite bundle has phases.validation.status = "PASSED" while summary.validation = "partial" (verified from the JSON), so a gate reading phases.validation would also accept it. That inconsistency is tracked in result-validation-phase-status-contradicts-summary.
